bibliography.title: CLEAR: Context-Aware Learning with End-to-End Mask-Free Inference for Adaptive Video Subtitle Removal

abstract_sentences.text: Video subtitle removal aims to distinguish text overlays from background content while preserving temporal coherence.

evidence.anchor: distinguish text overlays from background content

abstract_sentences.text: Existing diffusion-based methods necessitate explicit mask sequences during both training and inference phases, which restricts their practical deployment.

evidence.anchor: explicit mask sequences during both training and inference

abstract_sentences.text: In this paper, we present CLEAR (Context-aware Learning for End-to-end Adaptive Video Subtitle Removal), a mask-free framework that achieves truly end-to-end inference through context-aware adaptive learning.

Our two-stage design decouples prior extraction from generative refinement: Stage I learns disentangled subtitle representations via self-supervised orthogonality constraints on dual encoders, while Stage II employs LoRA-based adaptation with generation feedback for dynamic context adjustment.
Notably, our method only requires 0.77% of the parameters of the base diffusion model for training.

On Chinese subtitle benchmarks, CLEAR outperforms mask-dependent baselines by +6.77dB PSNR and -74.7% VFID, while demonstrating superior zero-shot generalization across six languages (English, Korean, French, Japanese, Russian, German)—a performance enabled by our generation-driven feedback mechanism that ensures robust subtitle removal without ground-truth masks during inference.

experimental_design.name: Baselines and common masks
experimental_design.description: ProPainter, MiniMax-Remover, and DiffuEraser use official implementations/default hyperparameters; baseline masks are generated from Xsub and Xclean pixel differences.

experimental_design.name: Evaluation metrics
experimental_design.description: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DISTS, VFID, TWE, TC, Flow Mean, and Flow Variance are grouped into four metric categories.

experimental_design.name: Data and benchmark
experimental_design.description: The paper states over 160,000 pairs and a 400-random-sample benchmark, then separately describes 500 Stage-I pairs and 500 Stage-II samples.

experimental_design.name: Training configuration
experimental_design.description: Eight GPUs, PyTorch 2.0, bfloat16, Wan2.1-Fun-V1.1-1.3B, AdamW, batch settings, and training durations are supplied.

experimental_design.name: Seeds and run replication
experimental_design.description: No random seed, repeated-run count, or run-level uncertainty treatment is stated in §4.1--§4.2.

experimental_design.name: Data split and provenance
experimental_design.description: The text does not state train/validation/test split construction, source permissions, or how the three reported data scales relate.

ablation_inventory.name: Component progression
ablation_inventory.description: Table 2 adds M1 Stage-I focal weighting, M2 context distillation, M3 context-aware adaptation, and M4 context consistency; PSNR rises 21.62 to 26.80.

ablation_inventory.name: M1 adverse metric reversal
ablation_inventory.description: M1 improves PSNR but VFID changes 34.74 to 38.21 and DISTS 0.088 to 0.091; nearby prose emphasizes cumulative PSNR gains without explaining this reversal.

ablation_inventory.name: Inference hyperparameters
ablation_inventory.description: Table 3 varies denoising steps, CFG, and LoRA scale; 5 to 10 steps increases PSNR but worsens TWE and doubles time.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Explicit trade-off reporting
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: Table 3 and its text acknowledge better PSNR at 10 steps alongside worse TWE and doubled time.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Positive-summary focus after M1 reversal
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: The main table exposes worsened VFID/DISTS after M1; adjacent prose summarizes component gains through PSNR and final synergy without a separate explanation of those worse values.

adverse_presentation_strategies.name: Qualitative-only cross-lingual evidence
adverse_presentation_strategies.description: The paper uses figures for the six-language claim and does not give a language-wise quantitative table; this records evidence scope, not author intent.

measurement_disagreements.name: Parameter-efficiency configuration conflict
measurement_disagreements.description: Abstract/conclusion say 0.77%; Figure 3 says rank 8, about 112M, 0.8% of 14B; implementation says 1.3B and rank 64, and Table 1 says rank 64.

measurement_disagreements.name: Alpha schedule conflict
measurement_disagreements.description: Figure 3 calls the schedule triangular with period 30; Eq. (16) is a sine form; implementation calls it triangular with period 40 and gives no transform constraining the sine to [5,15].

measurement_disagreements.name: VFID percentage cannot be reconstructed from listed baselines
measurement_disagreements.description: The text says -74.7% VFID; Table 1's lowest baseline VFID is 72.51 versus CLEAR 20.37, which gives about 71.9%, and no denominator is specified.

measurement_disagreements.name: Cross-language caption conflict
measurement_disagreements.description: Main text/Figure 1 list German among six languages; appendix A3--A5 captions list Arabic, while p.15 artwork labels German.

final_judgment.single_storyline: CLEAR learns a noisy training-time prior from paired subtitled/clean video, then internalizes adaptive weighting in LoRA diffusion so inference accepts Xsub without external masks.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the two-stage causal chain, losses, Algorithm 1, baseline condition, benchmark statement, Table 1, component ablation, and hyperparameter trade-offs.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A restates the pipeline and Appendix B adds qualitative figures; it does not add data provenance, per-language metrics, uncertainty, failure cases, or parameter auditing.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 3 plus Eq. (14)--(22), Algorithm 1, and Table 2 let a reader trace Mprior to Mpred to weighting to component evidence.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Rank, backbone size, parameter percentage, and alpha schedule conflict, while cross-lingual evidence is qualitative and its captions disagree.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For noisy auxiliary signals, use them as training-time soft supervision, let the generation loss update a lightweight weighting head, and test each component separately.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule needs one auditable configuration for backbone, adapter rank, parameter fraction, schedule, and timing scope; otherwise mechanism claims and reproducibility diverge.

layout_analysis.column_format: Two-column ICML layout; cross-column figures/tables interrupt text flow, Figure 3 occupies much of p.4, and p.13--15 are visual-heavy appendix pages.
